To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a new method for the chiral analysis of 1 and its O-acetylated derivative 2 in wine using stable isotope labelled standards, and that the method was validated and applied to a number of commercial wines.
we developed and validated a sensitive and robust HPLC-MS method with SIDA for the enantiomeric profiling of 3-sulphanylhexan- 1-ol and its O-acetyl derivative in wine.

we have developed a novel chiral high-performance-liquid-chromatography-tandem-mass-spectrometry method using stable-isotope-dilution analysis for the quantification of the individual enantiomer of 3-sulfinylhexan-1 -ol and its O-acetyl derivative in wine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a novel chiral method for the analysis of the potent wine thiols, 3-sulphanylhexan- 1-ol (1) and its acetate (2).
developing a sensitive and selective analytical method for chiral analysis of 1 and its O-acetylated form 2 in wine.
the development of a sensitive, accurate and robust analytical method for the quantitation of the enantiomer profile of 1 and its acetate ester 2 in wines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the newly developed method provides a sensitive, robust, and accurate means of quantifying the enantiomeric profile of 1 and/or 2 in wine.

the method developed in the present work has been validated and successfully used to determine the enantiospecific concentrations of 3-SH and 3-SHA in a number of wine matrices, which is a significant step forward in the understanding of these compounds in wine.
the newly developed method can be used as a reliable tool for the chiral analysis of 1 and/or 2 in wine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the developed method is suitable for the chiral analysis of 1 and/or 2 in wine.
the newly developed method is a reliable tool for the chiral analysis of 1 and its acetate in wine, and the results of the enantiomeric analysis of 3-SH and 3-SHA are presented for the first time.
the newly developed HPLC-MS method is suitable for the determination of 1 and/or 2 in wine and can be applied for the determination of their enantiomeric ratios in wine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enantiomer ratios of 1 and its acetate 2 are highly variable in different commercial wines and are not related to the geographic origins of these wines.

the method can be successfully applied to determine the individual enantiomer concentrations of 1 and/or 2 in wine samples, and can be used to determine the enantioselectivity of 1 and its O-acetyl derivative 2.
3-SH and 3-SHA are present in a wide range of wines at levels ranging between 0.2 and 3 ng L- 1.
